stem: Solution **Y** is hydrochloric acid, $\text{HCl}\text{(aq)}$. Solution **Z** is aqueous 4-chlorobutanoic acid, $\text{Cl(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}\text{(aq)}$. The p$K_\text{a}$ of $\text{Cl(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}\text{(aq)}$ is 4.52. The pH of both solutions is 4.00.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Write an expression for the $K_\text{a}$ of $\text{Cl(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Write a mathematical expression to describe the relationship between $K_\text{a}$ and p$K_\text{a}$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Calculate the ratio.

$$\frac{[\text{HCl}] \text{ dissolved in solution } \mathbf{Y}}{[\text{Cl(CH}_2\text{)}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}] \text{ dissolved in solution } \mathbf{Z}} = \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A buffer solution of pH 5.00 is produced by adding sodium propanoate to 5.00 g of propanoic acid in $100\text{ cm}^3$ of distilled water.

Calculate the mass of sodium propanoate that must be used to produce this buffer solution. The $K_\text{a}$ of propanoic acid is $1.35 \times 10^{-5}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$.

[$M_\text{r}$: propanoic acid, 74.0; sodium propanoate, 96.0]

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some dilute sulfuric acid is mixed with a small sample of the buffer solution described in **(b)**. The final pH of the mixture is close to 1.

Explain this observation.
